newsitem.title: USA: BPA says Intertie hike delayed by power line work.
newsitem.headline: BPA says Intertie hike delayed by power line work.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said Friday it will not be able to immediately raise capacity on the Pacific Intertie due to a problem on a 500 kilovolt (KV) segment of the system.

On Wednesday, a contractor working on the John Day-Slatt line in Oregon flipped a crane because of muddy conditions, delaying eventual re-energizing of the line, Perry Gruber, a spokesman for BPA explained.
No estimate was available for when the 500 KV line would be back in service.
"We had expected to be able to raise the capacity as soon as we could, but we will have to wait," Gruber noted.
The John Day-Slatt line is crucial to BPA's ability to raise the interstate transmission system rate, he said.
Earlier Friday the Western Systems Coordinating Council gave final approval to plans to boost intertie capacity by about 25 percent to 6,250 MW.
The lines have been capped at 5,200 MW, out of a rated capacity of 7,900 MW, since last August, after two major power blackouts hit the western U.S.
